title: String Immutability & The Intern Pool
contentMarkdown:
Strings in Java are immutable value objects backed by byte arrays. String literals are automatically pooled in the JVM String Constant Pool on the heap.

Calling `new String("val")` forces a new heap allocation, whereas `"val".intern()` returns the canonical reference from the pool.
keyTakeaways: String pool lives in heap memory since Java 7.
Avoid redundant new String("...") allocations in hot loops.

quiz.prompt: Given: String a = "dev"; String b = new String("dev"); What does (a == b) evaluate to?
quiz.explanation: 'a' points to the string literal in the constant pool, while 'b' is a newly created instance on the heap. Reference equality (==) returns false.

options.text: false, because 'b' references a distinct heap instance while 'a' references the pool
true, because the compiler automatically deduplicates identical string contents
